ideas.description: Exploit. Tests a proposed new child of H2.3: accuracy is set mainly in the final 32 px phase, so the 28 px middle phase can be dropped cheaply. On the E015 recipe (Muon, Lookahead/EMA, CUDA graphs, 9 epochs, last group 512), change only the resolution schedule from 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps to 24/32 px at 70/30% of steps. The 32 px tail keeps exactly its current step count and position, so the LR and EMA schedules stay the same. Build no longer needs the 28 px graph; keep the 24 and 32 px warm-up and capture, and keep error_on_recompile on after build.
ideas.expected: Time falls about 8% (2.7 epochs move from about 0.71 to 0.51 s/epoch, saving about 0.5 s), to about 6.0-6.15 s. Accuracy changes by -0.1 to -0.5 pp, to about 0.753-0.756. A loss of 0.3 pp or less beats the epoch dial (about 1.9 s/pp) and supports the tail-sets-accuracy reading of E011. A loss above 0.5 pp means the middle phase matters too, so resizing should stop here.

ideas.description: Exploit, testing W5's crux (is accuracy set in the 32 px phase?) against a uniform epoch trim. On the E015 recipe, cut 0.75 epoch from the 24 px phase only: 3.6 → 2.85 epochs at 24 px, with the 28 px (2.7 epochs) and 32 px (2.7 epochs) phases unchanged in absolute length. Total is 8.25 epochs. Stretch the LR and Lookahead/EMA schedules to the new total step count, as in E008. Compiled shapes are unchanged; error_on_recompile stays on. If I-swap (24/32 only) is kept first, apply the same 0.75-epoch cut to its 24 px phase instead.
ideas.expected: Time falls about 5.5-6% (about 0.38 s), to about 6.2 s. That is the same saving as a uniform 0.5-epoch trim, which E008 showed costs about 0.18-0.27 pp. If accuracy is set in the tail, the loss is 0.15 pp or less (about 0.755-0.757). A loss of 0.25 pp or more means early epochs count as much as late ones, and plain uniform trims are the right dial.

ideas.description: Diagnostic, making no recipe change. It answers the W1/W3/W5 crux on whether E015's 0.7574 is real margin or a kernel reshuffle. (1) Rebuild E015 from scratch (fresh inductor cache) and run it twice through ar.py. Check that max-autotune with cudagraphs reselects the same kernels, giving bit-identical per-seed accuracies on seeds 0-2. (2) Run the same build offline on held-out seeds 3-12 through the harness code path (benchmark.run --seed 3 --n 10). Record the per-seed accuracies, mean, std and the offset from 0.7574. Do not edit submissions/arena/.
ideas.expected: Time is unchanged at about 6.58 s (±1%). If autotune is stable, seeds 0-2 are bit-identical across rebuilds. If not, the kept tip's local accuracy is itself noisy (±0.14 pp), and later keep decisions need wider margins. The held-out mean is about 0.753-0.756 (E010 config: 0.7540). If it is at least 0.755, the tip has room for about 0.5 epoch of trimming. If it is at most 0.753, every trim must first buy accuracy back.

ideas.description: Explore. Tests whether bs 2000 (copied from CIFAR-10 airbench94_muon) is too large for a 225-step CIFAR-100 run. On the E015 recipe, change only the batch size from 2000 to 1250 (40 steps per epoch exactly, so no ragged batch; 360 steps instead of 225). Keep the per-step Muon lr at 0.24 and momentum at 0.6; E014 showed the lr is flat over 0.24-0.36, so the extra steps' larger total movement is tolerated. Scale the SGD-group lrs with batch size the way the code already does. Express the resizing and EMA/Lookahead schedules as fractions of total steps. Recapture every resolution's CUDA graph at the new batch shape in build, with error_on_recompile.
ideas.expected: Time rises 2-5% (per-step fixed cost is about 1.4 ms × 135 extra steps, plus slightly lower kernel efficiency), to about 6.7-6.9 s. Accuracy rises 0.1-0.6 pp. The idea pays off only with a gain of at least 0.35 pp, which buys about 0.75 epoch (7%) in the next trim. A gain under 0.2 pp means bs 2000 is fine; discard.

ideas.description: Exploit, the third point of the optimizer grid (LS and lr were flat). On the E015 recipe, change only the Muon momentum for the conv filters from 0.6 to 0.8 (still Nesterov). The SGD groups, lr, wd, batch size, schedules, epochs and Lookahead/EMA stay the same. Since momentum is a Python constant baked into the graph, recapture every resolution in build.
ideas.expected: Time is unchanged (±1%). Accuracy moves between -0.3 and +0.4 pp. A gain of at least 0.3 pp supports H1.5.1 and funds about 0.75 epoch. A loss of 0.2 pp or more means 0.6 is near-optimal or high, and the grid should stop.

ideas.description: Explore, aimed at the biggest FLOP block. Group 2 (16×16 maps, 384 channels) is about half of the conv FLOPs, whereas the last group (narrowed in E010) is only about a quarter. On the E015 recipe, narrow only group 2 from 384 to 320 channels. Keep group 1 (128) and group 3 (512), the Muon lr, epochs, the resizing schedule and Lookahead/EMA unchanged. Recapture all shapes in build.
ideas.expected: Time falls 8-12% (to about 5.8-6.05 s). Accuracy falls 0.3-0.8 pp, so the run is likely infeasible on its own. The exchange rate decides the outcome: 2.5 s/pp or better (for example 0.6 s for 0.25 pp) beats the epoch dial (about 1.9 s/pp), and the narrower net should then be paired with an accuracy booster or a +0.25-epoch top-up. A rate below 1.9 s/pp means widths should stay put.

structured_output.summary:
The tip is E015 (6.58 s, 0.7574). Its effective margin is closer to E010's held-out 0.754, because the E015 accuracy gain is a kernel reshuffle. E012 settled the cost picture: time is about 95% conv work that scales with pixel count. Fixed and first-epoch cost is negligible. Systems trims beyond I021 can win at most about 1-2%. So the remaining time levers are fewer pixel-epochs and narrower widths, and each has to be paid for in accuracy. LS, Muon lr and the final-LR floor were all flat.

**New exploit ideas**
- **Swap 28→24 px, keep the 32 px tail at 30% (priority 5):** about -8% time. It tests D002/E011's reading that the full-resolution tail, not total pixels, sets accuracy.
- **Trim 0.75 epoch from the 24 px phase only (priority 4):** cuts the same time as a uniform 0.5-epoch trim, which separates "late epochs matter more" (W5's crux) from a uniform dial.
- **Rebuild plus held-out-seed diagnostic on E015 (priority 3):** answers the W1/W3/W5 crux and H4.1.1 by checking whether max-autotune kernel choice is stable across rebuilds and what the tip's true mean is.
- **Muon momentum 0.8 (priority 2):** the third grid point.

**New explore ideas**
- **Batch size 1250 (priority 3):** checks whether 225 steps is too few for CIFAR-100.
- **Group 2 from 384 to 320 channels (priority 2):** group 2 is the largest FLOP block, and this measures its exchange rate against the epoch dial.

**Existing queue**
- I021 (graph breaks, consensus about -1%) and I022 (plain EMA, which answers W5's crux on averaging) stay.
- I019 is still running.
- Nothing is dropped: no queued idea has a settled hypothesis or a harm forecast.

The queue now holds 8 ideas.
